```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Netterberg 2019 analysed serum atezolizumab PK, plasma biomarkers and tumor
size in 88 patients with relapsed / refractory non-small cell lung cancer
(NSCLC) from the phase I study PCD4989g. Two models are packaged from the
paper:

* `Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_il18_tgi` -- the final framework of the
  paper's Figure 3: two-compartment PK, an effect-compartment-driven pool
  indirect-response model for interleukin-18 (IL-18), a tumor-size model
  driven by the cycle-specific exposure and by the relative change from
  baseline in IL-18 at day 21, and the dropout model.
* `Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_itac` -- the same PK model with the pool
  indirect-response model for interferon-inducible T-cell alpha
  chemoattractant (ITAC), the second biomarker the paper modelled.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_il18_tgi"))$reference`
* Description (IL-18 / tumor model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_il18_tgi"))$description`
* Description (ITAC model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_itac"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.1198> (open access, PMC6704358)

# Population

The biomarker and tumor analyses used 88 patients with relapsed / refractory
NSCLC who received atezolizumab as a 30-60 min IV infusion every 3 weeks at
10, 15 or 20 mg/kg or 1,200 mg (one patient received 1 mg/kg). The PK model
was developed on 167 PCD4989g patients dosed at 10, 15 or 20 mg/kg and its
individual estimates were carried into the biomarker and tumor models. Baseline
covariates (Supplementary Table S5): number of metastatic sites median 2 (range
0-4), liver metastases 30%, never smokers 19% (current 11%, former 69%),
ECOG 0 / 1 28% / 72%, non-squamous histology 76%. Median baseline tumor size
(sum of the longest diameters, SLD) was 5 cm and the median tumor-assessment
duration 18 weeks (range 0-153). The paper does not tabulate age, weight, sex
or race.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_il18_tgi")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Collected:

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl`, `lvc`, `lq`, `lvp` | CL 0.233 L/day, Vc 3.35 L, Q 0.452 L/day, Vp 3.36 L | Supplementary Table S3 (also the Figure S2 legend) |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | IIV 42%, 27% | Supplementary Table S3 |
| `propSd` | 18.7% | Supplementary Table S3 |
| `lkin_il18`, `lkout_il18` | Rin 23.0 pg/mL/day, kout 0.106 1/day | Table 1, IL-18 model |
| `lbl_il18_pool`, `lslope_il18`, `lke0` | Pool0 499 pg/mL, Slope 0.168 mL/ug, ke0 4.36e-3 1/day | Table 1, IL-18 model |
| `etalkout_il18`, `etalbl_il18_pool`, `etalslope_il18` | IIV 47%, 78%, 80% | Table 1, IL-18 model |
| `propSd_il18` | 22.3% | Table 1, IL-18 model |
| `lkin_itac`, `lkout_itac` | Rin 3.07 pg/mL/day, kout 7.91e-3 1/day | Table 1, ITAC model |
| `lbl_itac_pool`, `lslope_itac` | Pool0 271 pg/mL, Slope 0.0599 mL/ug | Table 1, ITAC model |
| `etalkin_itac`, `etalbl_itac_pool` | IIV 48%, 115% | Table 1, ITAC model |
| `propSd_itac`, `addSd_itac` | 28.3%, 51.8 pg/mL | Table 1, ITAC model |
| `lrbase_tumor_size`, `lrgrowth` | SLD0 4.75 cm, RGrowth 0.0169 cm/week | Table 1, TGI model |
| `lkshr_drug`, `llambda_drug` | KShr,Drug 2.75e-6 L/mg/day/week, lambdaDrug 0.0609 1/week | Table 1, TGI model |
| `lkshr_il18` | KShr,IL-18 0.00282 1/week | Table 1, TGI model |
| `e_lmet_rgrowth`, `e_met_ge3_rbase_tumor_size` | 8.48, 0.927 (as 1 + theta) | Table 1; Results quote 0.16 vs 0.017 cm/week and 9.1 vs 4.8 cm |
| `kshr_drug_smoke_never` | 0 fixed | Table 1; Results "set to 0 in the final model" |
| `etalrbase_tumor_size`, `etalrgrowth`, `etalkshr_drug`, `etalkshr_il18` | IIV 62%, 93%, 124%, 181% | Table 1, TGI model |
| `propSd_tumor_size` | 13.4% | Table 1, TGI model |
| `lhaz_base`, `e_tumor_size_rcfb_hazard` | h0 0.0306 1/week, beta 1.56 | Table 1, dropout model |
| Pool indirect-response ODEs, `krel = kout * BioM0 / Pool0` | -- | Eq. 3 |
| Effect compartment, `ke1 = ke0`, CE(0) = 0 | -- | Eq. 4 and Methods |
| Tumor-size ODE | -- | Eq. 1 |
| `AUCcycle,n = Dose_n / CL_i` | -- | Eq. 2 |
| RCFB of IL-18 at day 21, zero before day 21 | -- | Methods, Tumor growth inhibition model |
| Dropout hazard `h0 * exp(beta * x)` | -- | Eq. 5 and Results |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. Four arms of 100 virtual patients receive
10, 15 or 20 mg/kg or 1,200 mg every 3 weeks as 1-h infusions for 28 cycles.
Body weight (needed only for the mg/kg arms) is not reported; it is drawn
log-normally around 70 kg. Liver metastases and never-smoking status follow
Supplementary Table S5 (30% and 19%). The share of patients with more than two
metastatic sites is not reported (median 2, range 0-4); 30% is assumed.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190201)
n_per_arm <- 100L
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,         ~mgkg, ~flat,
  "10 mg/kg",   10,    NA,
  "15 mg/kg",   15,    NA,
  "20 mg/kg",   20,    NA,
  "1,200 mg",   NA,    1200
)

subjects <- arms |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n(), log(70), 0.2), 40), 130),
    dose_mg = ifelse(is.na(flat), mgkg * WT, flat),
    MET_GE3 = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.30),
    LMET = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.30),
    SMOKE_NEVER = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.19),
    DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG = dose_mg
  )

n_cycles <- 28L
tau <- 21
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 21, by = 0.5), 1 / 24,
  seq(21, 585, by = 3.5),
  seq(189, 210, by = 0.25)
)))

make_events <- function(subj, obs_cmt) {
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = tau * (seq_len(n_cycles) - 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central", amt = dose_mg, rate = dose_mg * 24)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = obs_cmt, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, evid, cmt, amt, rate, arm, WT, MET_GE3, LMET, SMOKE_NEVER, DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG)
}

# Observation rows name an ODE state that is also a declared endpoint, so
# rxode2 returns every endpoint (Cc, il18, tumor_size / itac) on each row.
events_il18 <- make_events(subjects, "tumor_size")
events_itac <- make_events(subjects, "itac") |> filter(time <= 210)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subjects$id))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod_il18 <- readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_il18_tgi")
mod_itac <- readModelDb("Netterberg_2019_atezolizumab_itac")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190202)
sim_il18 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_il18, events = events_il18, keep = c("arm", "DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG"),
  sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
sim_itac <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_itac, events = events_itac, keep = "arm",
  sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
arm_levels <- arms$arm
sim_il18$arm <- factor(sim_il18$arm, levels = arm_levels)
sim_itac$arm <- factor(sim_itac$arm, levels = arm_levels)
```

Residual error is switched off (`sigma = NA`), so the profiles are
individual predictions with between-subject variability only.

## Atezolizumab PK

```{r pk-profile}
# Compare with Figure S2 of Netterberg 2019 (pcVPC of the PK model by dose).
sim_il18 |>
  filter(time >= 1 / 24, time <= 63, arm != "1,200 mg") |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(Cc, 0.025), Q50 = median(Cc), Q975 = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "Atezolizumab (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles. Compare Figure S2 of Netterberg 2019."
  )
```

## IL-18 and ITAC

```{r biomarker-profile}
# Compare with Figure 1b,c of Netterberg 2019 (pcVPCs to day 175).
bind_rows(
  sim_il18 |> transmute(id, arm, time, biomarker = "IL-18", conc = il18),
  sim_itac |> transmute(id, arm, time, biomarker = "ITAC", conc = itac)
) |>
  filter(time <= 175) |>
  group_by(biomarker, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(conc, 0.025), Q50 = median(conc), Q975 = quantile(conc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "Concentration (pg/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles, all arms. Compare Figure 1b,c of Netterberg 2019."
  )
```

The paper describes IL-18 and the other biomarkers as peaking at around day 21
and declining over later cycles, while ITAC stays elevated after six cycles;
the pool depletion (IL-18) and the slow ITAC turnover (kout 7.91e-3 1/day)
reproduce both patterns.

```{r biomarker-rcfb-by-dose}
# Compare with Figure 2 of Netterberg 2019 (relative change from baseline by
# nominal dose, protocol sampling days).
nominal_days <- c(1, 7, 21, 42, 63, 126)
bind_rows(
  sim_il18 |> transmute(id, arm, time, biomarker = "IL-18", conc = il18),
  sim_itac |> transmute(id, arm, time, biomarker = "ITAC", conc = itac)
) |>
  filter(arm != "1,200 mg") |>
  group_by(id, biomarker) |>
  mutate(rcfb = 100 * (conc - conc[time == 0][1]) / conc[time == 0][1]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(time %in% nominal_days) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(time), rcfb, fill = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-50, 400)) +
  scale_fill_grey(start = 0.9, end = 0.4) +
  labs(
    x = "Nominal time after first dose (days)", y = "Relative change from baseline (%)",
    caption = "Compare Figure 2 of Netterberg 2019 (IL-18 and ITAC panels)."
  )
```

## Exposure and IL-18 metrics that drive tumor shrinkage

The tumor model uses two individual metrics: the cycle exposure
`AUCcycle,n = Dose_n / CL_i` and the relative change from baseline in IL-18 at
day 21, `RCFB_IL-18,d21`. Netterberg 2019 reports the 5th, 50th and 95th
percentiles of both in the analysis dataset (Figure 4 legend; median AUC
`5,600 mg/l*day` and median RCFB 0.43 in the Results).

```{r driver-percentiles}
drivers <- sim_il18 |>
  filter(time == 42) |>
  select(id, arm, auc_cycle, rcfb_il18_d21)

all_drivers <- drivers
driver_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("AUCcycle (mg*day/L)", "RCFB IL-18, day 21"),
  sim_p05 = c(quantile(all_drivers$auc_cycle, 0.05), quantile(all_drivers$rcfb_il18_d21, 0.05)),
  sim_p50 = c(median(all_drivers$auc_cycle), median(all_drivers$rcfb_il18_d21)),
  sim_p95 = c(quantile(all_drivers$auc_cycle, 0.95), quantile(all_drivers$rcfb_il18_d21, 0.95)),
  pub_p05 = c(2900, 0.21),
  pub_p50 = c(5600, 0.43),
  pub_p95 = c(9500, 1.34)
)
driver_tab |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    Metric = metric,
    "Simulated 5th" = sim_p05, "Simulated median" = sim_p50, "Simulated 95th" = sim_p95,
    "Published 5th" = pub_p05, "Published median" = pub_p50, "Published 95th" = pub_p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated (all four arms pooled) vs published percentiles of the tumor-model drivers.")

drivers |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    "Median AUCcycle (mg*day/L)" = signif(median(auc_cycle), 3),
    "Median RCFB IL-18, day 21" = signif(median(rcfb_il18_d21), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Arm = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated medians by arm.")

auc_1200 <- median(drivers$auc_cycle[drivers$arm == "1,200 mg"])
stopifnot(
  # 1,200 mg flat dose: the median AUC is 1,200 / CL, independent of the
  # assumed weights; a mis-transcribed CL or dose unit moves it far more
  # than 20% from the published dataset median.
  abs(auc_1200 / 5600 - 1) < 0.2,
  # Median IL-18 day-21 response: the published value is a median of
  # empirical Bayes estimates, which shrink towards the typical value.
  median(all_drivers$rcfb_il18_d21) > 0.25,
  median(all_drivers$rcfb_il18_d21) < 0.65
)
```

The published median AUC lies between the simulated 15 and 20 mg/kg arm
medians, and the published 5th percentile is close to the 10 mg/kg median; the
analysis dataset's mix of dose levels is not reported, so the pooled
simulated percentiles (equal arm sizes) are not expected to match exactly.
The simulated
`RCFB_IL-18,d21` distribution is centred slightly lower than the published
one; the published percentiles summarise individual estimates from the
observed patients, whereas the simulation draws new patients from the
estimated distributions under an assumed weight distribution.

## Replicating Figure 4: tumor-size simulations

Figure 4 shows the typical SLD time course of a current / former smoker with
two or fewer metastatic sites and no liver metastases after 1,200 mg every 3
weeks, varying either `RCFB_IL-18,d21` (left; AUC 5,600 `mg*day/L`) or AUC
(right; `RCFB_IL-18,d21` 0.43). In the packaged model AUC is set through the
cycle-dose column (`DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG = AUC * CL`, with the typical CL), and
a given `RCFB_IL-18,d21` is obtained by choosing the individual whose IL-18
pool and slope random effects (shifted together) produce it -- the tumor model
sees only the resulting day-21 value.

```{r figure-4-helpers}
fig4_times <- seq(0, 90 * 7, by = 1)
fig4_events <- function(auc) {
  dose <- auc * 0.233
  d <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, rate = dose * 24, cmt = "central", ii = tau, addl = 30) |>
    rxode2::et(fig4_times, cmt = "tumor_size") |>
    as.data.frame()
  d$id <- 1L
  d$MET_GE3 <- 0
  d$LMET <- 0
  d$SMOKE_NEVER <- 0
  d$DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG <- dose
  d
}
solve_typical <- function(shift, auc) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_il18, events = fig4_events(auc),
    params = c(lbl_il18_pool = log(499) + shift, lslope_il18 = log(0.168) + shift),
    omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}
rcfb_gap <- function(shift, target, auc) {
  s <- solve_typical(shift, auc)
  s$rcfb_il18_d21[s$time == 42] - target
}
shift_for_rcfb <- function(target, auc) {
  uniroot(rcfb_gap, interval = c(-2, 2), target = target, auc = auc, tol = 1e-6)$root
}
```

```{r figure-4}
scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel,                 ~label,                    ~rcfb, ~auc,
  "Impact of IL-18 on SLD", "RCFB = 0.21 (5th)",      0.21,  5600,
  "Impact of IL-18 on SLD", "RCFB = 0.43 (50th)",     0.43,  5600,
  "Impact of IL-18 on SLD", "RCFB = 1.34 (95th)",     1.34,  5600,
  "Impact of AUC on SLD",   "AUC = 2,900 (5th)",      0.43,  2900,
  "Impact of AUC on SLD",   "AUC = 5,600 (50th)",     0.43,  5600,
  "Impact of AUC on SLD",   "AUC = 9,500 (95th)",     0.43,  9500
)
fig4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  sc <- scenarios[i, ]
  s <- solve_typical(shift_for_rcfb(sc$rcfb, sc$auc), sc$auc)
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = sc$panel, label = sc$label, week = s$time / 7,
    sld = s$tumor_size, rcfb = s$rcfb_il18_d21, auc = s$auc_cycle
  )
}))
fig4$label <- factor(fig4$label, levels = unique(scenarios$label))
fig4$panel <- factor(fig4$panel, levels = unique(scenarios$panel))

ggplot(fig4, aes(week, sld, linetype = label, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3, 5.5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "SLD (cm)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Netterberg 2019."
  )
```

The paper's text gives the median-scenario landmarks: a nadir at about 27
weeks and a return to the baseline tumor size by 89 weeks. The other values
below were read off Figure 4 by the maintainers.

```{r figure-4-check}
fig4_summary <- fig4 |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(
    rcfb_d21 = rcfb[which.min(abs(week - 6))],
    auc = auc[1],
    nadir_cm = min(sld),
    nadir_week = week[which.min(sld)],
    sld_week89 = sld[which.min(abs(week - 89))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,                  ~fig_nadir_cm, ~fig_nadir_week, ~fig_sld_week89,
  "RCFB = 0.21 (5th)",     4.25,          25,              4.93,
  "RCFB = 0.43 (50th)",    4.20,          27,              4.72,
  "RCFB = 1.34 (95th)",    3.87,          50,              3.91,
  "AUC = 2,900 (5th)",     4.57,          19,              5.16,
  "AUC = 5,600 (50th)",    4.20,          27,              4.72,
  "AUC = 9,500 (95th)",    3.67,          34,              4.15
)
fig4_cmp <- left_join(fig4_summary, digitised, by = "label")
fig4_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    Scenario = label, "RCFB IL-18, day 21" = rcfb_d21, "AUC (mg*day/L)" = auc,
    "Nadir (cm)" = nadir_cm, "Nadir week" = nadir_week, "SLD at week 89 (cm)" = sld_week89,
    "Figure nadir (cm)" = fig_nadir_cm, "Figure nadir week" = fig_nadir_week,
    "Figure SLD at week 89 (cm)" = fig_sld_week89
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-patient tumor-size landmarks vs Figure 4 of Netterberg 2019.")

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solve against values read off the figure:
  # the tolerance covers the digitisation, not model noise.
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$nadir_cm - fig4_cmp$fig_nadir_cm) < 0.08),
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$sld_week89 - fig4_cmp$fig_sld_week89) < 0.08),
  # Paper text: nadir at ~27 weeks for the median scenario.
  abs(fig4_cmp$nadir_week[fig4_cmp$label == "RCFB = 0.43 (50th)"] - 27) < 3
)
```

## Tumor size with dropout

The dropout model gives each virtual patient a dropout time; tumor sizes after
it are discarded, as in the paper's pcVPC.

```{r tumor-vpc}
dropout_time <- sim_il18 |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    t_drop = {
      u <- runif(1)
      j <- which(surv_dropout < u)[1]
      if (is.na(j)) Inf else time[j]
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sld_obs <- sim_il18 |>
  left_join(dropout_time, by = "id") |>
  filter(time <= t_drop, time %in% c(0, seq(42, 585, by = 42)))

sld_obs |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Q10 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.10), Q50 = median(tumor_size), Q90 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "SLD (cm)",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles of patients still in the study. Compare Figure 1a of Netterberg 2019."
  )

median_drop_weeks <- median(dropout_time$t_drop) / 7
median_drop_weeks
```

The simulated median dropout time, `r round(median_drop_weeks, 1)` weeks,
compares with a median tumor-assessment duration of 18 weeks in the trial plus
the 3 weeks the paper assumed between the last assessment and dropout.

# PKNCA validation

Netterberg 2019 reports no NCA table. The PK model is checked with PKNCA over
cycle 1 (Cmax, AUC0-21) and over cycle 10 at steady state, where the dosing
interval AUC must equal `Dose / CL` -- the identity the paper's Eq. 2 uses for
`AUCcycle,n`.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_il18 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm))
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, arm) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, arm, time)

dose_df <- events_il18 |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 189),
  end = c(21, 210),
  cmax = c(TRUE, TRUE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)

nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(arm, start, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(
    Arm = arm, "Interval start (day)" = start, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "AUC over the interval (ug*day/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters by arm (cycle 1 and cycle 10).")
```

```{r nca-closed-form}
ss_check <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", start == 189) |>
  left_join(drivers |> select(id, auc_cycle), by = "id") |>
  mutate(ratio = PPORRES / auc_cycle)
summary(ss_check$ratio)
stopifnot(
  # Same individual parameters on both sides; the gap is trapezoidal error
  # plus the residual approach to steady state at cycle 10.
  abs(median(ss_check$ratio) - 1) < 0.03,
  quantile(abs(ss_check$ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.06
)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(arm = "1,200 mg", auclast = 5600)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res |> as.data.frame() |> filter(start == 189, arm == "1,200 mg"),
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*day/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20,
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated steady-state AUC over the cycle-10 dosing interval, days 189-210 (1,200 mg arm), vs the median AUC of the analysis dataset (Netterberg 2019 Results). * differs by >20%.")
```

The published median AUC (5,600 `mg*day/L`) pools the 10-20 mg/kg and 1,200 mg
patients, so the comparison with the 1,200 mg arm is approximate; the typical
value is 1,200 / 0.233 = 5,150 `mg*day/L`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 1 and Supplementary Table S3 report IIV as CV% of
  log-normal random effects; the variances use `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. If
  the percentages were instead `100 * omega`, the wide rows would change
  materially (KShr,IL-18 181%: 1.45 vs 3.28; KShr,Drug 124%: 0.93 vs 1.54).
  The paper does not say which convention its table uses.
* **Residual error.** The data were log-transformed with additive error on the
  log scale (proportional for PK, IL-18 and tumor size; additive plus
  proportional for ITAC). These are encoded as proportional and combined
  additive + proportional error on the linear scale.
* **Cycle dose as a data column.** `AUCcycle,n = Dose_n / CL_i` reads the
  cycle dose from the column `DOSE_ATEZOLIZUMAB_MG`, which must match the
  `amt` of the dosing records. Inside the ODE right-hand side rxode2's
  `podo()` / `dose()` return the infusion rate rather than the amount for an
  infused dose, so the dose cannot be recovered from the dosing records there.
* **IL-18 at day 21.** The paper fed the individual model-predicted
  `RCFB_IL-18,d21` into the sequentially fitted tumor model. The packaged
  model computes it in the same solve: the state `il18_d21` follows IL-18 up
  to day 21 and then holds that value. Day 21 and the waning AUC effect both
  count from the first dose, which must be at time 0.
* **Dropout predictor.** The paper names the predictor only as "the
  model-predicted change from tumor size at baseline". It is encoded as the
  relative change, `(SLD - SLD0) / SLD0`, which keeps `beta` dimensionless.
  The simulated median dropout time is similar under an absolute (cm)
  reading, so the trial's median follow-up does not separate the two.
* **Never smokers.** Table 1's `theta KShr,Drug-Non-Smoking = 0 fixed` is read
  with the Results text as the AUC-related shrinkage rate constant itself
  being 0 in never smokers, not as a fractional change of 0.
* **Units of the tumor model.** RGrowth, KShr,Drug, KShr,IL-18, lambdaDrug and
  h0 keep the paper's per-week units in `ini()` and are divided by 7 in
  `model()`, whose time unit is days. `RCFB_IL-18,d21` is a fraction (median
  0.43), not a percentage, despite the "1/(% week)" unit printed for
  KShr,IL-18; only the fraction reproduces Figure 4.
* **ke0.** The effect-compartment rate constant (4.36e-3 1/day, a half-life of
  about 160 days) is used as printed; with the depleting precursor pool it
  still produces the observed IL-18 peak near day 21.
* **Virtual cohort.** Body weight and the share of patients with more than two
  metastatic sites are not reported and are assumed (log-normal around 70 kg;
  30%). The PK model has no covariates, so weight only sets the mg/kg doses.
* **Not packaged.** The biomarker screen, the alternative tumor models of
  Supplementary Table S4 and the ITAC-driven tumor variants were not final
  models. The other six prioritised biomarkers (CRP, CD40, ICAM-1, IL-8,
  VCAM-1, proliferating CD8+ T cells) were not modelled.
